recipes.name: Hot Pepper Jelly
ingredients_raw: 2.5 cups finely chopped red bell peppers
1.25 cups finely chopped green bell peppers

steps.text: Sterilize six 8-ounce canning jars and lids according to the manufacturer's instructions. Heat water in a hot water canner.
Place bell peppers and jalapeño peppers in a large saucepan over high heat; stir in vinegar and fruit pectin.
Bring to a rolling boil, stirring constantly. Stir in sugar; bring back to a rolling boil, stirring constantly. Allow to boil for 1 minute, then remove from the heat and skim any foam off the top.
Quickly ladle jelly into sterile jars, filling to within 1/4-inch of the tops. Cover with flat lids and screw on rings tightly.

Place jars in the rack and slowly lower jars into the canner. The water should cover the jars completely and should be hot but not boiling. Bring water to a boil; cover the canner and process for 5 minutes.

raw_recipe.headline: Hot Pepper Jelly
raw_recipe.description: This hot pepper jelly recipe made with bell peppers and jalapeños is a deliciously sweet and spicy treat served on cheese or whatever you like!

video.description: In this video, Nicole shows you how to make homemade pepper jelly. This southern staple recipe uses diced bell peppers and jalapeños to make a sweet and tangy jelly spread. After stirring and boiling the peppers in a sauce pan with apple cider vinegar, fruit pectin, and sugar, add the mixture to sterilized glass containers. Once the jars have been sealed, let them sit in the simmering water to finish the process. Whether it’s spread on a cracker or a burger, this multi-purpose jelly should be in every kitchen.

review.reviewBody: This is a great recipe, but after making it twice, have found it either has a typo or needs a slight modification. Both times I have made this jelly as the recipe states, it has not set up properly, as others have noted as well. The first time I put it all back into a pan, added 1 more box of powdered pectin, cooked and processed again as stated. After that it set up fine and was absolutely delicious. I just made it again (as written) and am again having the problem with it not setting up. I will add more pectin and re-process as I did before and hope for the same results. For all first time users of this recipe...this is a fantastic flavored jelly...if you want it sauce consistancy follow the recipe as written. If you want jelly consistancy use 2 packets of pectin. And one word of warning...this stuff is addicting!!! I have also played with the type of peppers...substituting hotter peppers for or adding to the jalepenos. My latest batch is actually a 4 pepper jelly...Red, Green, Jalepeno and a touch of hablano...mmmmmm!

I just made this recipe today. Peper Jelly is the only thing I can every year. With that said, I used this recipe because it called for powdered pectin and I normally use liquid pectin. I have never used powdered pectin until today. 
Of course I changed a few things...First of all, I used only jalapeno pepper, 2lbs. I removed most of the seeds but left some for a little heat. Next, put all the peppers in my food processor with half the vinegar. Then I added the pepper mixture to my large stock pot with the remaining vinegar and added one box, 1.75 oz, of the powder pectin. The rest of the recipe I followed to the "T" with the exception of doubling the other ingredients...WITH THE EXPECTATION IF THE PECTIN...I only used the 1.75 oz box. I have read that some other users cant get their jelly to set. Mine worked perfect! I think the key that might be getting missed is that when you add the sugar, make sure it returns to a full boil. It takes a little while for the mixture to return to a boil. DO NOT add the sugar and let it sit for one minute...get it back to boiling. Considering that I doubled the recipe but used a single recipe amount of pectin and it worked...I think this recipe is great! I think I actually like the powder form better then the liquid. This jelly is delicious with some cream cheese and crackers. It's a great appetizer to have for the holidays when you have guests over.

I looked at many recipes before deciding to give this one a try and I am so glad I did. The only changes I made was 3 1/2 cups combination of red/ yellow/ orange bell peppers and 1/2 cup jalapeno peppers. We like the heat. I did use a thermometer after adding the sugar and boiled to 220- degrees. It set up beautifully and was thick enough while filling jars to have the peppers dispersed nicely. The taste is amazing! Wonderful recipe. I really think getting to a true rolling boil and using a thermometer is the key! Yumm

Delicious! Mine set up fine. Nice and thick, I used the inverted method, and it set fine. I made mine with a kick, delicious, but pretty hot. I used the ingredient formula as originally posted, although I changed the pepper ratio. Using the 4c pepper, 1c apple cider vinegar, 5c sugar and 1 pack of Sure Gell. However, I used 1c each bell pepper, Jalapeno and Red Cayenne; 1/2c each Hungary wax and Habanero. Hand cut or chopped. I actually cut my hot peppers two days ago, and they were resting in the refrigerator (I make hot sauce), until I could pick up some pectin. I did measure the peppers into a bowl with paper towels to absorb any excess liquid. I read page after page of reviews, forming a game plan as this was my first pepper jelly. I followed the instructions with the peppers and vinegar first, a few minutes on high then added the pectin, cooking that to a rolling boil, and boiled about 2 more minutes. It totally looks like it will never work, as someone else had mentioned. I added the sugar and brought that to a rolling boil, I then cooked that for 2-3 minutes (after reading reviews to cook it longer), I could see it getting thicker, like pudding does. It only made 5 -8oz jars, I believe cooking it longer, and hand chopping vs food processor varies the actual amount of peppers. I used the inverted method and just have to run warm water over the jars to release the jelly as it set quite hard.

I saw all the reviews about not setting up so I used a thermometer and made sure it got to 220 degrees Fahrenheit and kept it there for a minute before pulling to fill jars. I did use Hoosier Hill Farm fruit pectin and it set perfectly. I used 2 cups red bell peppers, 2 cups jalapeno peppers, the taste was perfect for me, but my DH could have used more heat.

This jelly is amazing! I doubled the recipe since I was making enough to give away for gifts and here are the amounts that I used:
-6 cups green bell pepper, chopped fine
-2 cups jalapenos, chopped fine
-2 cups apple cider vinegar
-2 packages (1.75 oz) powdered pectin (I used Sure Jell)
-10 cups white sugar

1 - Mix chopped bell peppers, jalapenos, apple cider vinegar and sure jell in large pot over HIGH heat.
2 - When it reaches a boil, BOIL for 3 minutes.
3 - Mix in sugar and continue to stir until sugar is melted.
4 - Bring to a rolling boil and continue stirring for 3 minutes. Remove from heat and set aside.
5 - Ladle jelly into jars. leaving 1/4 inch head space.
6 - Process jars for 10 minutes in hot boiling water bath.
7 - Cool jars overnight on counter and label.
8-Store in cool, dry place for up to 1 year.

Makes approximately 12 (1/2 pint) jars.

If following this recipe. . .make sure you use Sure Jell. . .because despite what the other reviews say. . .MY jelly turned out BEAUTIFULLY!

This is good stuff, of course I tweaked it. Cut back sugar to 4 cups and upped the hot peppers to 1/2 cup. I used 3 jalapeno and 4 habanero peppers to get there. Be sure to bring back to a boil after adding the sugar. I did not can this. It came out a perfect medium heat. Next time more habaneros!

I used only green bell peppers and jalapeños. Followed rest of recipe and jelly set up while still warm! The next time I food-processed 12 jalapeños (seeds and veins), one large yellow bell pepper (no seeds) in 1 1/2 cups of apple cider vinegar for 5 minutes then strained in a pot. I boiled the liquid for about 10 minutes until I got down to 2 cups of liquid. I then dissolved the pectin powder and used only 4 cups of sugar to get 7 X 4-ounce jars of jelly. Got a nice pale-green jelly that starts out tasting sweet then got a surprising after burn!

I've made this several times with slightly different results each time. I believe the batch I've just completed is the best so far. I've always just used whatever peppers I have on hand totalling 4 cups which include approximately 10 to 12 jalapeno peppers. I've read several comments about adding more pectin to obtain the correct consistency as 1 minute cook time is not sufficient. I just boil it for 10 minutes instead and it's the perfect consistency.

Fabulous recipe! Everybody I've shared with is going crazy over it! I am so glad I read the other reviews before making this. One of the reviewers stated he altered the peppers (hotter) but stayed at 5 cups total. I added two serrano peppers and additional jalapenos to reach the 5 cups after measuring my red and green peppers. I live at 4,593' altitude and used two packets of pectin. Worked great. I also adjusted the processing time to 7 minutes for my altitude (1 minute per 1,000' over 3,000').

I added 1/8 cup powdered crawfish boil seasoning and OMG talk about a hit. However, If you want it thick set like jelly you should let the peppers drain in a colander to get rid of excess moisture. If you prefer it a little runny then begin cooking immediately after chopping.

5 stars for this recipe! made small changes . instead of 1/4 cup of finely chopped peppers I made it with finely chopped fresh garlic. Chopped up both red and green peppers for a nice color Used 1 cup of white vinegar. It turned out with a beautiful clear green color with bits of colorful peppers. Taste is fabulous!
Made it per your recipe,Natalie. So good over cream cheese, on a cracker.

It set up beautifully! I used a food processor to finely chop the peppers and, while watery, it gave me a color that I love (it looks like a garnet). Now, I needed 8 (not 6) 8 ounce canning jars. Flavor is good, but will get better with time.

We loved this. So delicious and so pretty. I multiplied the recipe by 2.5. I used 2/3 jalapeno peppers and 1/3 yellow and red sweet peppers. I pulsed the peppers in the food processor with the cider vinegar so I would have small pieces of varying sizes (it helps keep the pieces throughout the jelly instead of floating up.) It set up beautifully and is just delicious, but I wish it was hotter! When I make it again, I will leave all the veins and seeds in the jalapeno peppers. Overall though, this is a pretty perfect recipe, and so easy to make.

Fan favorite with this recipe !! I use red, yellow , orange peppers with 3 jalapeños w/ seeds ! 4 cups of peppers, just use your favorite. I’ve made it a few times , last batch was only slightly set, tastes fantastic.. I just did another batch for gifts, I added an extra pectin .. perfect jelly!! I don’t have a canner so to speak but due process them in a deep pot, as long as the water covers the top of the jar, medium boil for about 5 mins .. set them in a tea towel on ur counter and wait for the pop !! Great easy peasy recipe !!
This was very good but would add another Pectin as want a Jelly type of thickness. Would also add more heat as we like it hot.
This is an easy recipe to follow. Our jelly turned out beautifully and we added the residual to our homemade bbq sauce to kick up the heat!
Second time making this, following directions exactly. It doesn’t set the way you’d expect; it’s slightly runny. Flavor is delicious though!
Didn’t set up enough but the taste was great!
